content.thinking:
The argument commits a logical fallacy: it says because aviation fuel prices rose AND petroleum derivative prices rose, therefore aviation fuel is a petroleum derivative. This is a classic correlation/causation fallacy - two things sharing a property (price increase) doesn't prove one belongs to the other category.

Option C points this out with a parallel example: food prices also rose, but that doesn't prove aviation fuel is food. This is the best evaluation because it exposes the logical flaw with a reductio ad absurdum.

The answer is C.

The answer is C. The argument commits a classic correlation fallacy — two things sharing a property (price increase) doesn't prove one belongs to the category of the other. Option C exposes this with a perfect parallel: food prices also rose, but that obviously doesn't make aviation fuel a food product.
